episodes.153014: Strong to severe thunderstorms developed across southeastern Kansas and northeastern Oklahoma during the late afternoon of the 14th, as a cold front approached the area. The thunderstorms moved east across the region through the evening hours. The strongest storms produced damaging wind gusts.
episodes.153771: A strong cold front moved across the region during the late afternoon and evening, and interacted with an unstable air mass and strong vertical wind shear to produce several rounds of strong to severe storms. Widespread wind gusts over 60 mph were reported across the region. The greatest damage occurred near Osage Beach and St. Robert, where straight-line wind gusts over 70 mph produced wind damage at a strip mall and damaged or destroyed manufactured homes.
episodes.154233: A strong storm system pushed a cold front across northern Utah. Thunderstorms developed along the front, and these storms produced some strong winds. In the wake of the frontal passage, a moist flow kicked off some mountain snows.

events.location: 3.22 WNW Salt Lake No Two Arp
events.narrative: A peak wind gust of 64 mph was recorded by the Baccus Highway sensor.
Multiple reports of wind damage associated with a thunderstorm were reported in Taylorsville.  A vinyl fence was damaged, a large tree was uprooted, and large limbs were downed.
